focus_ar: وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَكَانُوا۟ مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ
trigger_ar: وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ فَهُمْ لَا يَهْتَدُونَ
before: Satan beautifies their actions and turns the peoples from the path while they retain insight.
after: The repeated chain makes the paradox audible: the same deed beautification and obstruction leaves them unguided despite their insight.
reason: 27:24 repeats the focus's exact chain, وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ, then says فَهُمْ لَا يَهْتَدُونَ. Beside وَكَانُوا مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ, that ending sharpens the paradox: clear perception does not prevent diversion.

focus_ar: وَقَد تَّبَيَّنَ لَكُم مِّن مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ ۖ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ
trigger_ar: عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ كَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُۥ سُوٓءُ عَمَلِهِۦ وَٱتَّبَعُوٓا۟ أَهْوَآءَهُم
before: Visible ruins testify to the earlier peoples' error, while Satan makes their deeds attractive.
after: Clear evidence and attractive wrongdoing stand as opposing perceptual states, showing how awareness can coexist with misdirection.
reason: 47:14 sets عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ against زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ and وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْوَاءَهُمْ. Alongside the focus's تَبَيَّنَ لَكُمْ and مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ, the contrast shows how available clarity can coexist with the pull of beautified wrongdoing.

focus_ar: وَقَد تَّبَيَّنَ لَكُم مِّن مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ ۖ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ
trigger_ar: فَلَوْلَآ إِذْ جَآءَهُم بَأْسُنَا تَضَرَّعُوا۟ وَلَٰكِن قَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
before: The focus's ruined dwellings make the peoples' failed response legible to later witnesses.
after: Beautification follows hardened hearts under hardship, making the bad response a rejection of warning rather than a harmless mistake.
reason: In 6:43, بَأْسُنَا arrives, yet قَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ; then the same زَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ formula explains what they kept doing. This sequence makes the focus's adorned deeds part of resistance after warning, not an isolated lapse.

trigger_ar: وَصَدُّوا۟ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ زِدْنَٰهُمْ عَذَابًۭا فَوْقَ ٱلْعَذَابِ
before: The focus reports that the peoples were turned away from the path.
after: Obstructing the divine way carries a public consequence: their corruption compounds the punishment.
reason: 16:88 uses وَصَدُّوا عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ for the obstruction and immediately promises عَذَابًا فَوْقَ الْعَذَابِ. This adds a consequence to the focus's completed turning-away: blocking others from the way deepens the punishment.

focus_ar: وَقَد تَّبَيَّنَ لَكُم مِّن مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ ۖ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
trigger_ar: أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قَآئِمٌ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ نَفْسٍۭ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ ۗ وَجَعَلُوا۟ لِلَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ قُلْ سَمُّوهُمْ ۚ أَمْ تُنَبِّـُٔونَهُۥ بِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ أَم بِظَٰهِرٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ ۗ بَلْ زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مَكْرُهُمْ وَصُدُّوا۟ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ ۗ وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍۢ
before: The focus makes the old peoples' ruins visible evidence and describes how deception turned them from the path.
after: Their attractive schemes remain answerable under divine oversight, so deception does not cancel responsibility for the way they chose.
reason: 13:33 opens with قَائِمٌ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ, placing every earning under divine oversight; later زُيِّنَ مَكْرُهُمْ and صُدُّوا عَنِ السَّبِيلِ echo the focus's deception. Beside its manifest ruins, the focus can be heard as evidence in that moral account, not just a report of mistaken perception.

trigger_ar: زُيِّنَ لِفِرْعَوْنَ سُوٓءُ عَمَلِهِۦ وَصُدَّ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
before: The focus names ʿAd and Thamud as earlier peoples whose dwellings testify to their end.
after: The same misdeed-and-path pattern is attached to Pharaoh, extending the focus's catalogue to a named ruler.
reason: 40:37 attaches زُيِّنَ سُوٓءُ عَمَلِهِ to فِرْعَوْنَ and follows it with صُدَّ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ, matching the focus's beautification and diversion. Since 29:39 next names Pharaoh among another set of arrogant rulers, this gives the repeated pattern a specific face, though the mechanism is already clear from closer parallels.

focus_ar: وَقَد تَّبَيَّنَ لَكُم مِّن مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ ۖ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
trigger_ar: وَصَدُّوا۟ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَشَآقُّوا۟ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلْهُدَىٰ لَن يَضُرُّوا۟ ٱللَّهَ شَيْـًۭٔا وَسَيُحْبِطُ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ
before: The focus places clear evidence and perceptive capacity beside obstruction from the path.
after: The parallel makes guidance explicitly available before rejection and shows that obstructive conduct leaves its own works fruitless.
reason: 47:32 couples صَدُّوا عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ with مِن بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الْهُدَىٰ and سَيُحْبِطُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ. The focus likewise sets تَبَيَّنَ and مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ beside path-diversion; this ayah makes the prior availability of guidance explicit and shows the deeds losing their outcome.

trigger_ar: يُرِيدُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتَهَا نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ فِيهَا
before: The focus says the peoples' deeds themselves were made attractive to them.
after: Worldly life's ornament sits beside the deeds repaid within it, a loose echo of how desire colors conduct.
reason: 11:15 names زِينَتَهَا as something desired and then أَعْمَالَهُمْ as deeds repaid in worldly life. It never says those deeds are beautified or that anyone is diverted, so this is only a faint lexical and thematic echo.

focus_ar: مِّن مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ ۖ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ
trigger_ar: وَقَيَّضْنَا لَهُمْ قُرَنَآءَ فَزَيَّنُوا۟ لَهُم مَّا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلُ فِىٓ أُمَمٍۢ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلْإِنسِ
before: The focus presents ruined dwellings as evidence after communal misguidance.
after: The named ruins become part of a repeating history in which companions make the whole horizon attractive before judgment settles among earlier nations.
reason: In 41:25, قُرَنَاءُ beautify مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ, and the decree settles among أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ. The focus's عَادًا وَثَمُودَا and مَسَاكِنِهِمْ make those earlier nations concrete examples of that recurring pattern.

before: The focus says that even perceptive people were turned away from the way.
after: The Fatiha's daily plea for the straight path frames their history as a warning against trusting perception without asking for guidance.
reason: The focus says فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ immediately before مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ, while the Fatiha repeatedly places اهْدِنَا before الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ. That recited petition turns their history into a warning that clear sight alone does not secure the right way.
